transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 min
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luca Patel, Hannah Ortiz (Redwood); Priya Singh, Jason Ortega, Amira El-Amin, Tom Rivers (NovaQuay)

[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE for NovaQuay. Luca is our solutions engineer, Hannah on CSM, and from NovaQuay?
[00:08] Priya Singh (NovaQuay): Hi Maya, thanks. Priya here. Jason, Amira, Tom joining. Busy week but wanted to lock next steps for capacity and a possible multi-region top-up.
[00:15] Maya: Great. Agenda — current usage, desired uplift, region add (EU/AS), contract term extension, security questions, and scheduling a bench. Is that right?
[00:22] Jason Ortega (CTO): Yep. We're at about 6M tokens/day typical, spikes to ~18M over marketing pushes. Need predictability and lower p95 on generation latency for customer-facing flows.
[00:35] Amira (Devops): Also need VPC onboarding checklist redlined; we have strict KMS requirements.
[00:39] Luca (Redwood SE): Cool, thanks. Quick callout — from prior telemetry your mix is 70/30 chat vs embeddings; that influences batching and pooling decisions. We can recommend a mixed Dedicated pool for chat and Hosted for embeddings to save cost but still give throughput.
[01:05] Priya: The team prefers Dedicated for the chat lane but want autoscale/burst to hosted as fallback. Concerned about cold starts if we failover to hosted.
[01:15] Hannah (CSM): We have warm pool options and prefix KV cache strategies to reduce cold-start penalty; Luca can detail later.
[01:20] Tom (Procurement): On commercial, if we add EU and APAC nodes what's the uplift per region and is there a combined discount if we extend term?
[01:30] Maya: We'll send detailed numbers but ballpark — region add is a capacity multiplier plus a management fee. Term extension typically reduces unit price ~8-12% depending on committed tokens. We'll put options in an amended SOW.
[01:45] Jason: Latency — p50 is fine but p95 is our redline. We need p95 < 600ms for 512-token seqs. Can Redwood guarantee that in Dedicated?
[01:55] Luca: On Dedicated with appropriate GPU class and slotting, p95 sub-500 is achievable for 512 tokens for most Llama-ish variants; caveat is concurrency and batching. We'll propose a config with per-tenant slot isolation and rate shaping. Also fallback to smaller quantized variants in hosted if capacity saturated.
[02:20] Priya: Are there any model fallbacks that degrade quality noticeably? We can't have hallucination increase during bursts.
[02:28] Luca: Good question — we maintain a model catalog and specify quality tiers. Fallbacks attempt to preserve same checkpoint family; when switching to quantized or smaller models we tie a regression test suite to detect notable quality drift. We'll run those eval prompts as part of the bench.
[02:50] Amira: Security — we need SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence, audit logs, and HSM-backed key control; is that in Private or also in Dedicated?
[02:59] Maya: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS; audit logs and SAML SSO are supported. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for the highest sovereignty. For Dedicated we can provide SOC2 docs and an architecture diagram for your security team.
[03:15] Tom: Data residency — what happens to cached KV? Where is it stored?
[03:22] Luca: KV cache is ephemeral, resident on the inference node; for cross-region clusters we can limit KV residency to the requested region. Persisted caches (if you opt in) are encrypted and stored in region-bound storage controlled by your KMS.
[03:40] Priya: Great. About autoscale — can we set policy to allow X% burst to hosted only if latency threshold remains below Y? We want cost controls.
[03:52] Hannah: Yes, policies can be conditional — burst to hosted only if p95 < 800ms and cost per token below a set throttle. You can also set hard caps.
[04:08] Jason: For the bench — what telemetry will Redwood need?
[04:12] Luca: We'll ask for 7-day token histogram (time-of-day peaks), distribution of seq lengths, concurrency distribution, and a small prompt set for quality checks. Ideally a replayable trace for a 30–60 minute peak window.
[04:30] Priya: We can provide a masked dataset for quality evals. Performance traces maybe sensitive; we can share anonymized traces.
[04:36] Maya: That's fine, anonymized traces work. We'll produce a test plan — goal: validate p50/p95, cold-start delta, throughput, and quality regression.
[04:48] Amira: How long does region provisioning take? If we order EU cluster next week when would it be live?
[04:53] Maya: For Dedicated node provisioning in EU typically 3–4 weeks. APAC might be longer depending on capacity, 4–6 weeks. If you want faster, we can do a staged approach: start with hosted-backed EU nodes while Dedicated is ready.
[05:10] Jason: So a hybrid ramp. Works. On pricing, do we get a trial credit for the bench?
[05:16] Maya: We can provide a one-time benchmarking credit; I'll include that in the quote.
[05:22] Tom: Procurement timeline — we need all commercial by next Friday to hit our internal quarterly commit. Can Redwood meet that?
[05:28] Maya: Yes, we'll prioritize. I'll send a draft by Monday, finalize by Thursday/Friday.
[05:35] Priya: One more thing — SLA during bursts. If we have a multi-region failover, what are the SLOs?
[05:43] Luca: SLOs are region-specific. If primary region fails over, p95 may temporarily increase; we can set automatic fallbacks and circuit-breakers. We'll propose an SLA clause for failover behavior and a small credit for extended outages.
[06:00] Priya: Sounds reasonable. Do you have customers with similar patterns?
[06:04] Maya: Yes — a payments customer runs dedicated in us-west, with APAC hosted fallback; they use prefix caching to keep cold-starts low. We'll send an anonymized reference.
[06:15] Amira: On the technical bench — any change to model kernel selection between EU and APAC? Could that affect output variance?
[06:23] Luca: Slightly — different hardware generations pick different kernels. We quantify that in our model onboarding report; differences are usually within noise but we include sample outputs to surface any drift.
[06:40] Jason: For KMS integration — we need HSM and rotation policy support. Do you have an integration playbook?
[06:48] Hannah: Yes, we have a KMS/HSM integration checklist and RBAC mapping doc. We'll share both.
[06:54] Priya: Great. Let's talk numbers quickly — what uplift do you recommend for our 18M peak?
[07:00] Luca: For 18M token peaks with 512 avg seq we recommend a Dedicated pool sized for sustained 12M and a burst buffer to handle the remaining 6M via hosted. That keeps unit cost controlled and ensures p95 headroom. If you want lower p95 headroom increase Dedicated by ~20%.
[07:20] Priya: We'll consider. If we extend the contract by 12 months do the region add-ons get blended?
[07:25] Maya: Yes — term blending is possible, we'll show blended vs unblended pricing scenarios.
[07:33] Tom: Anything blocking from procurement side? We need the SOW and invoice cadence to match our PO process.
[07:39] Maya: We'll include Net30 and milestone-based invoices in the draft.
[07:45] Priya: Okay let's recap — action items?
[07:48] Maya: 1) NovaQuay to send histograms and masked prompts (Priya). 2) Redwood to send amended quote and SOW with EU/APAC options and bench credit (Maya). 3) Redwood SE to draft bench runbook and test plan (Luca). 4) Procurement to confirm timeline (Tom). Agreed?
[08:05] Jason: Agreed.
[08:08] Priya: One question on fallback quality — will Redwood throttle or degrade fidelity automatically or pause until Dedicated is available?
[08:17] Luca: Configurable — you can set policy to either auto-fallback with model-family equivalent, fallback to a lower cost quantized model with monitoring, or reject requests beyond capacity. We'll test behavior.
[08:33] Amira: Ok thanks. We'll aim to have histograms by April 1.
[08:38] Maya: Perfect. I'll ping the SOW Monday and book the bench window for week of April 6 — proposing April 7 10:00 UTC for a 90 minute run.
[08:50] Tom: Works for procurement too.
[08:53] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[08:55] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links: SOW draft, security pack, and bench runbook.
[09:02] Hannah: I'll drop the SOC2 and KMS checklist to your security channel.
[09:06] Priya: Appreciate it, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional proper names mis-heard; timestamps approximate.
